agents.title: Agents
agents.desc: Adding agents, job descriptions, skills, appearance and permissions live in the Agents section of the Organization page.
agents.manage: Add new agents and manage their roles and permissions from a single screen.

permissions.title: Dynamic Permission Matrix
permissions.desc: Decide what each agent can access. For CLI providers this matrix maps directly to the tool list and sandbox mode.
permissions.how: Agents start in the folder of the task's project (this project: {{workspace}}). For Claude Code, disabled permissions are removed from the --tools list; file writes are auto-approved with acceptEdits mode only in the workspace + extra folders. For Codex, --sandbox read-only / workspace-write is chosen. An agent with terminal permission can run any command in the shell — only enable it for agents you trust. If “Require approval” is on, an approval card appears in the left panel before the agent starts.
permissions.noWorkspace: no folder selected — CLI agents won't run

connections.title: Connection permissions
connections.desc: Server and database access per agent × connection. Default: no access. In Production, operations that change data also wait for your approval.
connections.empty: No connections yet. Add them under Organization → Connections.

providers.title: Providers
providers.desc: The model / CLI connections behind the agents. The default provider is used for every agent without its own provider.
providers.empty: No providers — agents run in demo mode.

kinds.claudeCli: Runs the official `claude` CLI in the background. File/terminal tools are enabled according to the permission matrix.
kinds.anthropic: Direct model call via the Messages API: no file system or terminal access; uses the app's file and connection tools.
kinds.openai: Model call via the Chat Completions API: no file system or terminal access; uses the app's file and connection tools.
kinds.codexCli: Runs OpenAI's `codex exec` command in sandbox mode.
kinds.mock: No key needed. Agents behave as if they were really working.

form.apiKeyNoSpaces: The key must not contain spaces.
form.apiKeyHint: Encrypted with the operating system keychain (Windows DPAPI) and stored in the local SQLite; never sent back to the interface.
form.claudeLogin: Run `claude auth login` once in a terminal to sign in (you can also do it from the Terminal tab).
form.codexLogin: Run `codex login` once in a terminal to sign in.

endpoint.label: Endpoint
endpoint.invalid: Not a valid address: use an http(s) URL without user, query or fragment.
endpoint.insecure: Use HTTPS; plain http is only allowed to this computer (localhost / 127.0.0.1).

hints.gemini: Gemini through its OpenAI-compatible API. Get a key in Google AI Studio.
hints.ollama: A local model served by Ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434 — start Ollama and pull a model first. Nothing leaves your computer.
hints.lmstudio: A local model served by LM Studio at 127.0.0.1:1234 — start its server and load a model first. Nothing leaves your computer.
hints.custom: Any server that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions API, e.g. a company gateway (…/v1). A key is sent only if you enter one.

memory.title: Persistent Memory
memory.desc: Context the lead and agents never forget. Every run adds the organization-wide records plus the project's most relevant ones (FTS5 + importance + recency) to the prompt.
memory.placeholder: E.g. Keep UI copy short; code comments in English.

semantic.title: Semantic memory
semantic.desc: Off: agents recall memories by matching words. On: memories are also found by meaning ("login error" finds "sign-in fails"). Uses the embeddings endpoint of an OpenAI-compatible provider: OpenAI, or a local Ollama / LM Studio so nothing leaves this computer.
semantic.modelHint: Embedding model, e.g. text-embedding-3-small or nomic-embed-text
semantic.noProvider: Add an OpenAI API provider (OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama or LM Studio) under Providers first.
semantic.stays: Local server: memory text stays on this computer.
semantic.leaves: Memory text is sent to this provider to be embedded (like any prompt to it).
semantic.error: Embedding failed, words only for now: {{error}}

folders.title: Project folders
folders.desc: Every project has its own folder: agents (CLI) work in the folder of the task's project, and the terminal opens there too.

startup.title: On startup
startup.desc: When the app opens, ask which projects to open or reopen the project tabs from the last session directly.

autopilot.title: Autopilot
autopilot.desc: Idle agents pick up the next tasks on their own.

review.title: Lead review
review.desc: Finished work is reviewed by the lead and either approved or sent back for revision.

twins.title: Share work between twins
twins.desc: A free agent takes over a task queued for a busy agent with the same role and skills (e.g. a duplicated developer). Tasks sent back with a review note stay with their agent.

race.title: Race mode
race.desc: When a task starts, a copy also goes to a free member on another provider or model; the lead keeps the better attempt and discards the other. Needs the lead's review. Costs about twice as much.

data.title: Data management
data.desc: All data lives in a single SQLite file on this computer. See how much space it takes, clean up old records, take backups or reset.

stats.filesSub_one: {{count}} original file · those used by backups are kept
stats.filesSub_other: {{count}} original files · those used by backups are kept

projects.title: Projects
projects.desc: Tasks, chat, logs and memory belong to a project; cleaning one project doesn't touch the others. Agents, teams and the files in the folder are kept.
projects.summary: {{tasks}} tasks · {{messages}} messages · {{logs}} logs · {{memories}} memories · {{decisions}} decisions · {{reports}} reports · {{files}} files ({{size}})

parts.memoriesHint: What agents remember from this project
parts.logsHint: Logs and finished runs (running jobs stop)
parts.filesHint: Attachments, agent outputs and folder records (files in the folder are not touched)

org.title: Organization and records
org.desc: Data not tied to a project.
org.memoryDesc: {{total}} records used across all projects (preferences, shared rules, {{decisions}} decisions).

retention.title: Log retention
retention.auto: Agent logs older than {{days}} days are deleted automatically at startup and every 6 hours.

backups.title: Backups
backups.desc: A snapshot of the database (settings, agents, organization, projects, tasks, memory). The last 10 backups are kept; one is taken automatically before a reset.
backups.restoreWarning: Current data will be backed up and replaced with this one; the app restarts.

reset.title: Factory reset
reset.desc: All running jobs are stopped. A backup is taken automatically first; if you reset by mistake you can restore it from Backups.

work.title: Delete work data only
work.desc: Tasks, chats, logs, decisions, reports, memory and file records of all projects are deleted (original files used by a backup stay until that backup is deleted; project folders are not touched).
work.keeps: Kept: agents, permissions, organization, teams, projects and their folders, providers, settings.

all.title: Reset everything
all.desc: The app returns to its freshly installed state: agents, organization, projects, providers and saved API keys are deleted too.
all.keeps: An empty organization and a single empty project remain; the setup wizard and the guide open so you can build the team from scratch. Files in project folders are not touched.

models.customHint: Type the exact name of a model that isn't in the list (e.g. a newly released one).
models.loading: Loading the models on your account…
models.liveError: Couldn't load your account's model list ({{error}}); showing the recommended list.
models.needKey: Enter the API key to also see the models on your account.
models.openaiNoGpt6: GPT-6 models aren't listed: Agentbits' OpenAI connection (Chat Completions) can't use tools with them. Use GPT-6 through Codex CLI.
models.cliAliases: Aliases always use the newest model of that family available to your account.

notes.opusplan: Opus plans, Sonnet does the work
notes.codexRecommended: recommended for complex coding and agent work

limits.title: Security and limits
limits.desc: Limits on what a single task run may spend, how long records are kept, and what agent CLIs inherit from your computer.

run.title: Per task run
run.minutesDesc: Stops a run that takes longer (wall clock, pauses included). The task waits for you. Empty = no limit.
run.tokensDesc: Stops a run once it has used this many tokens (input, cache and output). Empty = no limit.
run.costDesc: Stops a run once its reported cost reaches this amount. Only Claude Code reports cost, once per turn. Empty = no limit.

privacy.title: Records
privacy.auditDesc: Connection and app calls older than this are deleted automatically.
privacy.redactDesc: API keys, tokens, private keys and password=… values are masked before a transcript line is stored.
privacy.quotaDesc: Attachments and saved files are copied into the app’s data folder; adding more is refused past this size. Files in project folders don’t count. Empty = no limit.

env.title: Environment of agent CLIs
env.desc: Claude Code and Codex start with only what they need (PATH, user folders, proxy, language and their own CLAUDE_ / ANTHROPIC_ or CODEX_ / OPENAI_ variables). Other variables of your computer, such as cloud keys or tokens, are not passed. Add names here that your setup needs, e.g. AWS_PROFILE for Claude Code on Amazon Bedrock.
env.never: SSH_AUTH_SOCK, NODE_OPTIONS and ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE are never passed (the SSH agent would let an agent use your SSH keys without a connection permission).

errors.invalid: This setting value is not valid.
